nodes.title: Render the dialog into the body
nodes.why: The card's slide-in leaves a transform on it. A transform makes the card the containing block of every position: fixed element inside it, so a fixed backdrop drawn there covers only the card, and the card's overflow: hidden clips the rest. The body has no transform, so a backdrop portaled there covers the window whatever the card does.
nodes.alternative: Use the native <dialog> element and showModal().
nodes.tradeoff: showModal() puts the dialog in the top layer, closes it on Escape and makes the rest of the page inert, so it is a strong default for modals. The portal is the pattern many component libraries still use for every layer, and the labelling and focus work is the same either way.

nodes.title: Close only when the press and the release both land on the backdrop
nodes.why: The dialog sits inside the backdrop, so a click inside it bubbles to the backdrop's onClick; comparing target with currentTarget ignores it. A drag between the dialog and the backdrop, in either direction, fires its click on the backdrop too, because a click goes to the element that contains both the press and the release. Recording where mousedown and mouseup landed keeps a selection of the typed name from closing the dialog and wiping it.
nodes.alternative: Call stopPropagation in an onClick on the dialog.
nodes.tradeoff: Stopping the click hides it from document listeners that other code relies on, such as a menu that closes on any outside click, and it does nothing about the drag.

nodes.title: Keep the open dialog's side effects in one layout effect
nodes.why: The inert page, the locked body and the focus move exist only while the dialog is open. One effect keyed on open sets them, and its cleanup undoes them on every close and on unmount. A layout effect's cleanup runs in the same commit that removes the dialog, so the page is never inert after the dialog has gone, not even for one paint.
nodes.alternative: Set them in the open handler and undo them in each close path.
nodes.tradeoff: Every close path has to repeat the cleanup, and none of them runs on unmount: leaving the screen with the dialog open, through a route change, leaves modal-open on the body and the next screen unable to scroll.

nodes.title: Free the page before focusing the trigger
nodes.why: The cleanup removes inert before it moves focus back, because a button inside an inert element cannot take focus.
nodes.alternative: Focus the trigger in closeDialog, right after setOpen(false).
nodes.tradeoff: The cleanup runs only when React commits, after the handler has returned, so at that moment the page is still inert and the focus call does nothing. Focus is left on the body, and a keyboard user starts again from the top of the page.

nodes.title: Read the dialog's controls on every Tab
nodes.why: The delete button joins the tab order only once the typed name matches, so the last control changes while the dialog is open. Querying the enabled controls on each Tab always wraps at the real ends, and Tab between the middle controls stays with the browser.
nodes.alternative: Use a focus-trap library, such as focus-trap or react-focus-lock.
nodes.tradeoff: A library also handles focus that arrives from outside, through the browser toolbar or a click, and traps nested inside each other, at the cost of a dependency for the two key cases this dialog has.

nodes.title: Listen for Escape on the document while the dialog is open
nodes.why: A press on the backdrop leaves focus on the body, outside the dialog, so a keydown handler on the dialog would miss Escape. A document listener added while the dialog is open hears it wherever focus is, and isComposing leaves the Escape that cancels an input method's composition to the input.
nodes.alternative: Handle Escape in the dialog's onKeyDown.
nodes.tradeoff: It stays local to the dialog and needs no cleanup, but it misses Escape whenever focus has left the dialog.

nodes.title: Describe the button only while its tooltip shows
nodes.why: The tooltip renders only while it shows, and a reference to a missing id describes nothing, so the attribute comes and goes with the tooltip. useId gives each tooltip its own id.
nodes.alternative: Keep every tooltip in the DOM, hidden, and describe the button all the time.
nodes.tradeoff: A hidden description is part of the button's announcement from the first focus, where one added on focus can be read late or only on the next visit, depending on the screen reader. It costs an extra node per row, and the tooltip still needs placing when it shows.

nodes.title: Track hover and focus separately
nodes.why: A keyboard user who focused the button keeps the tooltip while the mouse passes over it and leaves, and Escape, heard on the document, hides a tooltip opened by hover too. Those are the persistent and dismissible parts of WCAG 2.1 success criterion 1.4.13.
nodes.alternative: One shown flag, set on enter and focus and cleared on leave and blur.
nodes.tradeoff: One flag is shorter, but a stray pointer closes the tooltip a keyboard user is reading.

nodes.title: Measure the tooltip in a layout effect
nodes.why: The first render puts the tooltip in the page, hidden, so it has a size. useLayoutEffect reads it before the browser paints, and its state update renders again before paint too, so the tooltip appears in place in the same frame as the hover or focus.
nodes.alternative: Measure in useEffect, or estimate the height from the text length.
nodes.tradeoff: useEffect can run after the browser paints (it does after a hover, which React does not treat as a discrete event), so the tooltip appears a frame late. An estimate breaks with another font, a zoom level or a translation.

nodes.title: Flip against the panel that clips the button

anchor.snippet: const fitsBelow = anchor.bottom + TOOLTIP_GAP + size.height <= boundary.getBoundingClientRect().bottom;

nodes.why: The rows scroll inside .settings, so the space that matters is the room left inside that panel. Below the panel the tooltip would cover the danger zone and lose its link to the row; positioning libraries such as Floating UI check the same clipping ancestors by default.
nodes.tradeoff: The window check is simpler and is right for a page that scrolls as a whole, but here it keeps the Log retention tooltip below the panel, over the delete section.

nodes.title: Follow panel scrolls while the button is in view
nodes.why: The tooltip is placed in the page, with the window's scroll offsets added, so it moves with the page when the window scrolls. A scroll inside .settings moves the button without it, so each panel scroll places the tooltip again while the button is inside the panel, give or take a pixel, including the scroll a browser makes to reveal a button it has just focused, and hides it once the button is partly scrolled out. A resize places it again too.
nodes.alternative: Hide the tooltip on any scroll of the panel.
nodes.tradeoff: Hiding is simpler and reads no layout while scrolling, but a keyboard user loses the tooltip whenever the browser scrolls a focused button into view.
